chief_complaint: recurrent painful oral and genital ulcers with uveitis
hpi_details: A 68-year-old female presents to the clinic with recurrent painful oral and genital ulcers with uveitis. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the painful ulcers in her mouth and private area are a severe recurrence of the cold sore virus or an allergic reaction to a new body wash.
concerns: She is worried that the persistent haze in her inflamed eyes will cause irreversible blindness and leave her unable to read or care for herself.
expectations: She hopes to receive a numbing mouth rinse so she can eat comfortably again and prescription eye drops to protect her vision.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Behçet Disease is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Active eye symptoms or suspected uveitis require urgent ophthalmology assessment because vision can be threatened; systemic treatment should be selected by the treating specialist according to organ involvement and severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: recurrent painful oral and genital ulcers with uveitis

Key HPI features: A 68-year-old female presents to the clinic with recurrent painful oral and genital ulcers with uveitis. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Examine oral/genital ulcers and skin lesions; assess joints and perform a focused neurologic and vascular review. Urgently assess visual symptoms.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Behçet Disease.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Herpes simplex virus infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Eye pain and vision changes — uveitis can threaten vision if untreated.
management_principles: Arrange urgent ophthalmology assessment for active eye symptoms or suspected uveitis.
Refer to rheumatology; systemic immunosuppressive treatment requires specialist direction and monitoring.
Assess for neurologic, vascular, and gastrointestinal involvement and escalate urgently when present.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient has recurrent painful oral and genital ulcers with reported uveitis; ask about eye pain, redness, photophobia, and vision change.
reference_soap.objective: Examine oral/genital ulcers and skin lesions; assess joints and conduct focused neurologic and vascular review. Evaluate visual symptoms urgently.
reference_soap.assessment: Behçet disease is a diagnostic consideration; alternative infectious and inflammatory causes require assessment.
reference_soap.plan: Arrange urgent ophthalmology evaluation for suspected active uveitis. Refer to rheumatology; systemic immunosuppressive treatment requires specialist direction. Escalate urgently for vision loss, neurologic symptoms, thrombosis, or other vascular involvement.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Behçet disease
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Behçet disease
Recognize vision-threatening and other organ-threatening features requiring urgent specialist assessment

teaching.one_liner: A variable-vessel inflammatory disease that can cause recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis, and vascular, neurologic, or gastrointestinal involvement.
red_flags: Eye pain and vision changes — uveitis can threaten vision if untreated

must_ask.say: How often do you get mouth sores, and how painful are they?
Have you had similar sores in the genital area?
Any eye pain, redness, or vision changes?
How often do these episodes recur?
Any other skin lesions, like red bumps on your legs?

history.answer: I keep getting very painful sores inside my mouth and down in my private area, and lately my eyes have become red and sensitive to light.
These sores first started appearing a few months ago, but this current severe flare started about a week ago and has been gradually worsening.
The sores are inside my cheeks, on my lower lip, and on my outer genital area, and both of my eyes are red and achy.
The sores are sharply stinging and burning, making it very painful to chew, swallow, or wipe myself, easily an eight out of ten in pain.
Each crop of sores usually lasts about one to two weeks before slowly healing, but new ones keep popping up every month or two.
Eating salty, spicy, or acidic foods and direct touch make the mouth sores sting terribly, while nothing specific seems to relieve them.
I have been feeling completely worn out with severe fatigue, and I noticed tender red bumps on my shins a few days ago.
No fever or chills, no night sweats, no unintentional weight loss, and no chest pain or shortness of breath.
My eyes are red, achy, and sensitive to bright light, and my vision has been slightly blurry over the past few days.
I have about three painful, round, whitish sores on the inside of my lips and cheek that make eating difficult.
There are two painful raw ulcers on my labia that burn intensely whenever urine touches them.
I noticed several painful red lumps on my shins and acne-like bumps on my back that showed up recently.
No numbness, weakness, tingling, severe headaches, or difficulty walking.
No leg swelling, calf pain, sudden redness, or symptoms of blood clots.
No stomach pain, chronic diarrhea, blood in my stool, or unintentional weight loss.
No pain with urination, blood in my urine, or abnormal vaginal discharge.
No swollen, red, or warm joints, although I felt some mild morning stiffness in my knees occasionally.
I had similar mouth sores a few times earlier this year, but this is the first time my eyes and private area have been this severely affected.
I tried salt water rinses and over-the-counter mouth ulcer ointment, but they provided only very temporary relief.
I haven't traveled anywhere, changed my diet, or been exposed to anyone with unusual infections.
The pain makes it hard to eat solid food and sleep comfortably, and I have had to cut down on my daily chores because of the exhaustion.
I thought maybe I picked up an awful strain of the cold sore virus or had a bad chemical reaction to a new body wash.
I'm terribly worried that this haze in my eyes won't clear up and I'm going to go permanently blind.
I really hope you can prescribe something to numb these mouth sores so I can eat, and drops to save my eyesight.
I have no history of high blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, or autoimmune conditions.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I am not taking any prescription medications, vitamins, or dietary supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only have half a glass of wine on special social occasions, maybe once a month.
I am a retired teacher and I live comfortably at home with my husband.
I have been married for forty years, in a monogamous relationship, with no new sexual partners and no history of sexually transmitted infections.
I went through menopause around age fifty and have had no vaginal bleeding or spotting since.
No one in my family has ever had recurrent ulcers, autoimmune diseases, or chronic eye problems.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable at rest, but squinting slightly due to light sensitivity.
Ciliary flush with conjunctival injection and mild photophobia in both eyes, with preserved extraocular movements and no gross visual field defects.
Multiple discrete, painful round ulcers with erythematous borders and yellowish necrotic bases on the inner buccal mucosa and lower lip.
Two tender, punched-out, shallow ulcerative lesions with yellowish bases on the labia majora without purulent discharge.
Tender, erythematous, warm subcutaneous nodules on both anterior shins consistent with erythema nodosum, and several sterile pustular papules on the upper back.
No active joint swelling, warmth, or deformity in bilateral knees, wrists, or ankles, with full range of motion.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact, including symmetric facial movement and normal pupillary light reflexes.
Normal symmetric motor strength and intact sensation throughout both upper and lower extremities.
Normal bilateral radial, dorsalis pedis, and posterior tibial pulses with no local bruits.
No calf tenderness, asymmetric swelling, erythema, or palpable cord along the lower extremity veins.
